title: Compatible pointed diagrams on corresponding admissible blowups
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $I\subseteq A$ an ideal, and $A'=\widehat A$ its $I$-adic completion, with canonical map $a:A\to A'$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Set $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$, $X'=\operatorname{Spec}A'$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $\mathcal J$ have as objects all finitely generated ideals $J\subseteq A$ with $\sqrt J=\sqrt I$, and let an arrow $J\to K$ be an actual $X$-morphism $Y_K\to Y_J$, where $Y_J=\operatorname{Bl}_J(X)$ [def-nagata-affine-blowup]. Write $Y'_J=\operatorname{Bl}_{JA'}(X')$ and $\rho_J:Y'_J\to Y_J$ for the canonical Rees blowup lift [def-nagata-strict-transform-blowup-comparison].

For an algebraically closed field $\Omega$, a compatible completion point system consists of geometric points $t_J:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to Y_J$ factoring over $\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)$, corresponding points $t'_J:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to Y'_J$ with $\rho_J t'_J=t_J$, and the corresponding domination maps $Y'_K\to Y'_J$ over $X'$ commuting with $\rho$ and the points [def-weil-geometric-point]. Put $H_J=\mathcal O^{\mathrm{sh}}_{Y_J,t_J}$, $H'_J=\mathcal O^{\mathrm{sh}}_{Y'_J,t'_J}$ [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit]. Include their ring diagrams $D,E:\mathcal J\to\mathbf{CRing}$, a natural transformation $\eta:D\to E$ and a structural transformation from the constant $A$-diagram to $D$. Their objects are exactly $H_J,H'_J$; their arrows and comparison components are the canonical pointed strict-local pullbacks of the domination maps and $\rho_J$ [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-functoriality], and their structural maps are those induced by $\operatorname{Spec}H_J\to Y_J\to X$. The object identifications, arrow equations and naturality laws are part of this presentation of the canonical diagrams, with no quotient-isomorphism condition.

Define $B=\varinjlim D$, $C=\varinjlim E$ and $u=\varinjlim\eta:B\to C$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. For a finite-generation witness for $I$, define $A\to B$ by the structural map at $J=I$ followed by its coprojection; define $A\to C$ by composition with $u$. These are the structural maps of the two colimits.
